data.name: Gangadhara
data.gender_notes: Gangadhara is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gangadhara refers to the deity who holds the Ganga river in his matted hair. According to Hindu mythology, this deity is an avatar of Lord Vishnu and is believed to bestow blessings of purity, protection, and salvation. The name Gangadhara carries the meaning “Lord of the Ganga” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gangadhara usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the ganga and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrier of the divine Ganga river
data.etymology: Gangadhara belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Ganga.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gangadhara total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
